title: Ethereum Gas Fee Estimator 2026 | Hacé Cuentas
description: Calculate Ethereum gas fees in ETH and USD. Estimate costs for transfers, ERC-20, Uniswap swaps, NFT mints, and DeFi. Compare L1 vs L2 savings.
intro: Gas is the computational cost of running anything on Ethereum — every opcode the EVM executes burns a tiny amount of it. You pay for gas in **gwei**, where 1 gwei = 10⁻⁹ ETH (one billionth). Your total cost in USD = `gas_units × gas_price_gwei × ETH_price × 10⁻⁹`. Different transactions burn different amounts: a plain ETH transfer is a flat 21,000 gas, an ERC-20 token transfer runs ~65,000, a Uniswap V3 swap typically lands between 150,000 and 300,000 depending on the route, an NFT mint sits around 200,000, and a complex DeFi action like a multi-hop swap plus deposit into Aave or a Pendle PT trade can blow past 500,000+ gas. Since the **London upgrade (EIP-1559, Aug 2021)**, gas price is split into a **base fee** that gets burned and a **priority tip** that goes to validators — `max_fee` is the ceiling you'll pay. This tool runs that math live so you can decide whether to send the tx now, wait for off-peak hours, or just bridge to an L2 like Arbitrum, Base, or Optimism and pay 50–100× less.
keyTakeaway: At 30 gwei and $3,000 ETH, a simple ETH transfer costs ~$1.89, while a complex DeFi interaction can exceed $45 — Layer 2s reduce those same fees to $0.10–$0.50.
useCases: Timing an NFT mint — check if 80 gwei mainnet drop is worth it vs waiting 6 hours for 20 gwei
Budgeting a $5k Uniswap swap — confirm gas isn't eating more than 0.5% of the trade
L2 vs L1 break-even — figure out if your $200 deposit justifies the L1 bridge fee or if you should just transact on Base directly
MEV-aware priority bid — set tip high enough to land in the next block during a competitive arb or liquidation
DeFi position rebalance — estimate gas across a 4-step claim/swap/deposit flow before pulling the trigger
Airdrop farming math — calculate total gas burn across 50 micro-transactions on L1 vs batching on zkSync
Teaching or documenting how EIP-1559 base fee and priority tip interact for a client or team
explanation:
## How Ethereum gas actually works in 2026

Gas is the unit Ethereum uses to price computation. Every EVM opcode — `SSTORE`, `CALL`, `KECCAK256`, `ADD` — has a fixed gas cost defined in the protocol. When you submit a transaction, your wallet multiplies the gas your tx will burn by the gas price you're willing to pay, denominated in **gwei** (1 gwei = 10⁻⁹ ETH).

Formula in plain math:

```
Fee (ETH) = gas_used × gas_price_gwei × 10⁻⁹
Fee (USD) = Fee (ETH) × ETH/USD
```

## EIP-1559 mechanics (post-London, Aug 2021)

Before EIP-1559, you bid blind in a first-price auction and routinely overpaid. Post-London, every block has a **base fee** that the protocol sets algorithmically:

- Base fee adjusts **±12.5% per block** based on how full the previous block was, targeting 50% blockspace utilization.
- The base fee is **burned** — it leaves circulating supply forever. This is the deflationary pressure the ETH ultrasound-money crowd talks about.
- On top of the base fee you set a **priority tip** (also called miner tip pre-Merge, now validator tip post-Merge) — this goes to the validator who proposes the block.
- Your `max_fee_per_gas` is the ceiling. You actually pay `min(max_fee, base_fee + priority_tip)`. If base fee spikes mid-block, you don't get rugged past your max.

This split is why MEV matters. During a liquidation cascade or popular NFT mint, searchers will jack priority tips into the hundreds of gwei to land first. If you're not bidding competitively, your tx sits in the mempool while builders pick the bag.

## Gas units by transaction type (2026 reference)

| Action | Typical gas | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| ETH transfer (EOA → EOA) | 21,000 | Hard-coded minimum |
| ERC-20 transfer | ~65,000 | Higher on cold storage slots |
| Uniswap V3 swap | 150,000–300,000 | Multi-hop routes use more |
| NFT mint (ERC-721) | ~200,000 | ERC-721A optimized mints can be lower |
| Aave deposit | ~250,000 | |
| Complex DeFi (swap + LP + stake) | 500,000+ | |

## Layer 2 reality check (post-Dencun)

**EIP-4844 / Dencun (March 2024)** introduced **blob transactions** for L2 data availability. This dropped L2 costs roughly **10×** overnight. Current typical fees in 2026:

- **Arbitrum One** — swap ~$0.10
- **Optimism** — swap ~$0.05
- **Base** — swap ~$0.05
- **zkSync Era** — swap ~$0.20
- **Scroll / Linea** — swap ~$0.10–0.30

Blob fees themselves are volatile — when many rollups post simultaneously, blob gas can spike, briefly pushing L2 swap costs to $0.50+. Check [L2Beat](https://l2beat.com) for live numbers.

## How to actually lower your gas bill

**1. Time it.** US East/West evening hours (roughly 9 PM – 4 AM ET) are usually the cheapest because European traders are asleep and US business-hour DeFi activity has died down. Weekends are quieter than weekdays. Check the Etherscan Gas Tracker (`etherscan.io/gastracker`) for live gwei — if base fee is under 15 gwei, you're in a window.

**2. Batch.** Use a multicall contract or aggregator (1inch, Matcha, CoW) so multiple actions execute in one tx. One 400k gas batched tx beats four 100k gas standalone txs because you only pay the 21k base + intrinsic gas once.

**3. Migrate to L2.** If you're not yet on Arbitrum or Base for day-to-day DeFi, you're leaving money on the table. The L1 bridge fee amortizes after 3–5 L2 transactions.

**4. Use gas tokens / CHI-style refunds** — mostly deprecated post-London, but some niche batching contracts still use gas-refund tricks.

## Looking ahead: Pectra and beyond

The **Pectra** upgrade (Prague + Electra) bundles several EIPs including EIP-7702 (account abstraction for EOAs — gas can be sponsored by dApps, paid in ERC-20s, batched natively), EIP-7251 (validator max effective balance to 2,048 ETH), and additional blob count increases that should further reduce L2 fees. For end users the biggest practical shift is **sponsored transactions** — onboarding flows where the dApp pays gas while you sign with your existing wallet.

## Tools to bookmark

- **Etherscan Gas Tracker** (`etherscan.io/gastracker`) — live base fee, priority fee, and tx cost estimates
- **Ultrasound.money** — track ETH burned per block
- **L2Beat** (`l2beat.com`) — live L2 fees, TVL, and bridge stats
- **Blocknative Gas Estimator** — mempool-aware predictions

## Limitations of this calculator

Gas estimates per tx type are medians; specific contract calls can use significantly more or less. ETH/USD and gwei move second-to-second — treat this as a planning tool, not a real-time oracle. L2 fees are conservative midpoints; check the specific rollup's explorer for exact numbers. We don't model MEV-boost priority tip spikes during congestion events.

faq.q: Why is gas so expensive sometimes?
faq.a: Demand spikes. The base fee adjusts ±12.5% per block targeting 50% blockspace utilization, so when blocks consistently fill up — popular NFT mint, major liquidation event, hot memecoin launch — base fee compounds rapidly. Add MEV searchers bidding aggressive priority tips on top and you get the 200+ gwei spikes you see during peak congestion. Once demand cools, base fee decays just as fast.

faq.q: When is gas cheapest on Ethereum mainnet in Eastern Time?
faq.a: Generally between 9 PM and 4 AM ET on weekdays, and most of Saturday/Sunday. That window catches the dead zone between Asian morning DeFi activity and US daytime. Live check Etherscan Gas Tracker before sending — sub-15 gwei is the threshold for 'gas is cheap right now' on L1. Holidays (US Thanksgiving morning, Christmas Day) can also be unusually quiet.

faq.q: What's the break-even for using Layer 2 vs Layer 1?
faq.a: Bridging to Arbitrum or Base costs roughly $3–8 in L1 gas one time. Each L2 transaction saves you ~$2–40 vs L1 depending on action complexity. Math: if you'll do 3+ transactions on L2 over the next month, bridge. For a single one-time $50 swap, L1 may still be simpler. For NFT minting, DeFi farming, or any recurring activity, L2 always wins.

faq.q: What priority tip do MEV bots actually bid?
faq.a: Variable. For normal periods, 1–2 gwei priority tip is fine. During a competitive arb, liquidation, or sniping opportunity, searchers will tip 50–500+ gwei to guarantee inclusion in the next block. If you're a normal user trying to land a swap during congestion, bumping priority tip from 1 to 3 gwei usually gets you in the next 1–2 blocks without burning excess.

faq.q: Does a failed transaction still cost gas?
faq.a: Yes. If your tx reverts on-chain — slippage too tight, insufficient liquidity, contract requirement not met — you still pay for all the computation the EVM ran up to the revert point. The asset transfer is rolled back, but gas is gone. Common painful examples: front-run Uniswap swap with slippage too low, NFT mint where supply sold out mid-block.

faq.q: Did Dencun (EIP-4844) lower mainnet gas fees too?
faq.a: Indirectly. Dencun (March 2024) introduced blob transactions that L2s use for data availability — this dropped L2 fees ~10× overnight, which migrated a lot of activity off mainnet. Less L1 congestion = lower L1 base fees on average. But on a per-tx basis, mainnet gas formulas are unchanged. The real win was L2 fees going from $0.50–2.00 down to $0.05–0.20.

faq.q: How will the Pectra upgrade affect gas?
faq.a: Pectra (Prague + Electra) bundles EIP-7702 (account abstraction for EOAs, enables sponsored tx and ERC-20 gas payment), EIP-7251 (validator MaxEB raised to 2,048 ETH, mostly a staking ops change), and potentially more blob throughput. For end users the practical wins are: dApps can pay gas for you, you can batch multiple actions natively without a smart wallet, and L2 fees should drop further as blob capacity expands.

faq.q: Can I just set gas price to 1 gwei and wait?
faq.a: Only if the current base fee is at or below your bid. Post-EIP-1559, the protocol-set base fee is the floor — if base is 25 gwei and you bid 1 gwei max, your tx will sit in the mempool forever and eventually get dropped. Most wallets enforce a sane minimum that adapts to current base fee. To pay the minimum reasonable amount, set max_fee = base_fee × 1.5 and priority_tip = 1 gwei during quiet periods.

faq.q: What's the difference between gas limit and gas used?
faq.a: Gas limit is the cap you authorize — the maximum the tx can spend before it auto-reverts. Gas used is what actually got consumed. You pay only for gas used; unused gas limit is refunded. MetaMask and other wallets auto-estimate a safe gas limit (usually estimated_gas × 1.2 for buffer). If you manually lower the limit too aggressively and the tx runs out of gas mid-execution, it reverts and you still pay for everything consumed up to that point.
